object.description: Large language models can extract text effectively but may hallucinate content absent from their source. Exact matching verifies contiguous spans, whereas discontiguous extraction depends strongly on tokenization and ordered alignment. LLM-specific subword tokenization with ordered alignment improves performance by about 50% over word-level tokenization, and taln implements this practical verification approach.

relations.statement: This publication contains this grounded claim.

evidence.span: Before tokenization, source and target text are normalized by applying Unicode normalization and ASCII translit- eration (unidecode), mapping several common punctuation/symbol variants to ASCII, and collapsing whitespace and newlines.

object.label: Voyager: exploratory single-cell genomics data analysis with geospatial statistics
object.description: Spatial organization is central to tissue function, and exploratory spatial data analysis can reveal structure in single-cell genomics data. Decades of geospatial methods have not been fully adapted to standard spatial-omics workflows. Voyager provides local, bivariate, and multivariate spatial methods through a common interface, a geometry-aware data structure, reproducible tutorials, and consistent R and Python implementations, revealing signals such as biologically relevant negative spatial autocorrelation.

object.label: Characterization of spatial homogeneous regions in tissues with concordex
object.description: Spatially resolved transcriptomics enables study of gene-expression variation across tissues, but cell-type spatial distributions confound identification of spatially variable genes. Analyses therefore need to distinguish cell-type-distribution effects from cell-type-independent spatial effects. concordex identifies cell-type-homogeneous domains efficiently across platforms and tissue types, facilitating decomposition of expression into cell-type and spatial variation and revealing subtle gene-variation patterns.
